understanding: The OKO repo already has a config-driven Ultralytics pipeline: UltralyticsDetector loads whatever `model_file` the YAML specifies (no version hardcoded), and configs/live-webcam.yaml currently points at models/yolov8n.pt with confidence 0.25 against camera device_index 0. The latest proof (runs/webcam-proof-capture.json) shows that 'before' baseline on device 0 producing a single low-confidence, likely-wrong detection ('surfboard' @0.28) and — critically — reading only 2 of 60 attempted frames. The task asks to swap in yolo11x (the largest YOLO11), tune the confidence threshold, re-run on device 0, and deliver a quantitative + visual before/after. The core engineering work is small (a config change plus a weights download); the real work is doing the comparison honestly and dealing with the fact that yolo11x is ~an order of magnitude heavier than yolov8n on an already frame-starved capture loop.
summary: Swap the config to yolo11x and tune confidence, but do the before/after as two honest tracks: (1) a reproducible labeled benchmark (COCO val or a small annotated subset) that yields real mAP/precision/recall/latency for yolov8n vs yolo11x, since those metrics are undefined on an unlabeled live feed; and (2) a live device-0 track where I record ONE short clip, replay it through both models for an apples-to-apples visual/quantitative comparison (read-rate, latency/FPS, detection count, mean confidence, annotated side-by-side frames), plus a true live run to prove no-error live processing. Choose the deployed confidence threshold from an F1/PR sweep on labeled data, not by eyeballing the webcam, and report inference cost candidly because 'maximum model' fights real-time throughput on this hardware.

decision_atoms.statement: Measure the before/after as two separate tracks — a labeled-dataset benchmark for true accuracy metrics, and a live device-0 run for latency/throughput/visual proof — rather than claiming mAP/precision/recall from the webcam.
decision_atoms.reason: mAP, precision and recall are only definable against ground-truth labels, which a live camera feed does not have; the success tests implicitly assume labeled metrics. Conflating the two would mean fabricating accuracy numbers from unlabeled footage.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires obtaining a labeled set (COCO val2017 or a small annotated subset) and more report structure; without it the accuracy half cannot be rigorous and must fall back to published COCO numbers.

decision_atoms.statement: Make the live comparison fair by recording one short clip from device 0 once and replaying it through BOTH yolov8n and yolo11x offline, plus a separate genuine live run to satisfy 'processes live input without errors'.
decision_atoms.reason: Two independent live runs see different scenes/lighting/motion, so any difference is confounded; identical replayed frames isolate the model as the only variable and make the result deterministic and reproducible.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a small capture/replay harness and decouples 'fair comparison' from 'live proof', so two artifacts are produced instead of one naive run.

decision_atoms.statement: Treat the model upgrade as a configuration change (model_file -> models/yolo11x.pt) plus a weights download, not a code rewrite.
decision_atoms.reason: UltralyticsDetector already reads model_file/confidence from config and lazily imports ultralytics; nothing pins a YOLO version, so the swap touches YAML, not detector code.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Minimal coding effort, but it means the bulk of effort/risk shifts to validation, weights provisioning, and performance measurement rather than implementation.

decision_atoms.statement: Pick the deployed confidence threshold from an F1 / precision-recall sweep on labeled data (per model), not by visual tuning on the webcam.
decision_atoms.reason: The current 0.25 threshold already yielded a probable false positive ('surfboard'@0.28); threshold directly trades precision against recall, so it must be chosen against ground truth to claim 'optimized'.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Needs the labeled set and a sweep step; the optimal threshold differs per model, so before/after must each use their own tuned value and that must be disclosed.

decision_atoms.statement: Measure and report inference cost up front, and flag that yolo11x may not run real-time on this hardware.
decision_atoms.reason: yolo11x is roughly an order of magnitude heavier than yolov8n, and the prior live run already read only 2/60 frames — a heavier model can worsen effective throughput, which is itself a recognition-quality outcome.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: 'Maximum model' conflicts with real-time on CPU-only hardware; mitigations (GPU/FP16, ONNX/TensorRT export, reduced imgsz) add scope, and honest reporting may show FPS regressing even as accuracy improves.

decision_atoms.statement: Anchor the accuracy claim with published COCO benchmarks (yolov8n ~37.3 vs yolo11x ~54.x mAP50-95), explicitly labeled as published — not as measured on device 0.
decision_atoms.reason: It gives a legitimate, citable quantitative delta for model capability even if a full local benchmark is out of scope, without dishonestly attributing those numbers to the live camera.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Published numbers reflect the COCO distribution, not this deployment's scene; they must be clearly separated from any locally measured figures to avoid overclaiming.

assumptions: The 'before' system is the current models/yolov8n.pt at confidence 0.25, as set in configs/live-webcam.yaml and recorded in runs/webcam-proof-capture.json.
Ultralytics is the inference framework and the model swap is config-level (UltralyticsDetector is already version-agnostic and config-driven).
Device 0 is the same webcam used previously, which was flaky (read 2 of 60 frames) and may be virtual/headless or capture-limited.
GPU availability is unknown; the plan must remain valid CPU-only and report latency honestly.
COCO 80-class pretrained weights are acceptable — no custom training or fine-tuning is in scope.
'Optimize confidence thresholds' means tuning inference-time conf/iou parameters, not retraining the model.
Network and disk are available to download yolo11x.pt (~109 MB) and, for the advanced track, a labeled validation set.

risks.risk: yolo11x is too slow on this hardware (likely CPU-only), so it cannot run near real-time and may read even fewer frames than the already-poor 2/60 baseline.
risks.mitigation: Benchmark latency before committing; offer GPU/FP16, ONNX/TensorRT export, or reduced imgsz; report FPS/read-rate transparently; keep yolov8n as a documented fallback and let the model stay config-selectable.

risks.risk: No ground truth on the live feed means mAP/precision/recall cannot be computed there, yet the success tests ask for them.
risks.mitigation: Compute those metrics on a labeled COCO val/subset; restrict live-camera claims to measurable quantities (read-rate, latency/FPS, detection count, mean confidence, visual correctness).

risks.risk: Camera device 0 is unavailable or flaky (prior run read only 2/60 frames), possibly virtual/headless, blocking the live proof.
risks.mitigation: Probe and warm up the camera, log the frame read-rate as a first-class metric, and fall back to a pre-recorded device-0 clip for the comparison if live capture degrades; surface the limitation rather than hide it.

risks.risk: A bigger model and/or a higher confidence threshold does not actually improve results for this specific scene — higher thresholds cut recall, and yolo11x may simply confirm the same objects.
risks.mitigation: Report precision and recall together and the threshold tradeoff; choose threshold by F1; present results across multiple scenes/lighting rather than one cherry-picked frame; state plainly if a metric did not improve.

risks.risk: Overfitting the comparison or threshold to a single scene/lighting condition, producing a misleading 'improvement'.
risks.mitigation: Capture several scenes/lighting conditions on device 0 and document the conditions; keep the replay clip and configs as reproducible artifacts.

risks.risk: Weights provisioning / dependency drift — wrong or unpinned ultralytics version, failed/checksum-mismatched download, disk pressure.
risks.mitigation: Pin the ultralytics version, cache and checksum-verify yolo11x.pt, and record the resolved versions in the report for reproducibility.

risks.risk: Privacy/consent — capturing and storing webcam footage of the user/environment.
risks.mitigation: Store artifacts locally only, obtain explicit consent, support face/region blurring in saved proofs, and never upload raw footage to external services.

minimal_version: pip install/upgrade ultralytics (pinned) and download yolo11x.pt. Add a config (or duplicate live-webcam.yaml) pointing model_file at models/yolo11x.pt with a chosen confidence. Capture ONE short clip from device 0, then replay the identical frames through the current yolov8n (before) and yolo11x (after). Produce a Markdown report with: side-by-side annotated frames, a table of measurable live metrics (camera read-rate, per-frame latency/FPS, detection count, mean confidence), and published COCO mAP for both models clearly labeled as published. Run yolo11x once truly live on device 0 to confirm error-free live processing and save that proof. Deliver before/after artifacts under runs/.
advanced_version: Everything in minimal, plus a reproducible labeled benchmark: run yolov8n and yolo11x over COCO val2017 (or a labeled subset) to compute real mAP50-95, precision, recall, and PR curves, with a per-model F1-optimal confidence-threshold sweep that drives the deployed value. Add performance engineering — GPU/FP16 and ONNX/TensorRT export with latency percentiles — and multi-scene/multi-lighting captures on device 0. Generate the report automatically with plots (PR curves, latency distributions, confidence histograms, class-wise breakdown) from a single reproducible script, archive all artifacts with explicit version pins and timestamps, and add a regression guard so any future model swap re-runs the same benchmark to keep the before/after comparison honest over time.
